name: LocalizationImporterWindow
src_typeComment: Toolkit > Localization Importer: turns a translator's spreadsheet into LocaleAssets plus the LocaleRegistry that lists them, and exports the round trip back out so new keys reach the translator.  Re-importing UPDATES the existing assets in place rather than replacing them, so their GUIDs survive and every scene reference to the registry keeps working — the whole point of doing this through the AssetDatabase instead of writing .asset files directly.

src_members.sig: public static string Import(LocalizationTable table, string outputFolder, string registryName, LocaleBundle metadata = null)
src_members.name: Import
src_members.comment: Public and static so the self-test can drive the whole import without a window open.  `metadata` is supplied only by a JSON bundle import. It is the reason a bundle CAN set a language's display name and system language while a CSV cannot: the bundle states them explicitly, so writing them is honouring the file, whereas a CSV import that touched them would be silently clobbering hand-set values with nothing.

src_members.name: BuildTableFromRegistry
src_members.comment: The union of every key in every locale, sorted — a key that only the newest language has still needs to reach the translator working on the others. Sorted rather than encounter-ordered so two exports of the same data produce byte-identical files and source control stays quiet.

src_members.name: EnsureFolder
src_members.comment: AssetDatabase.CreateFolder only makes ONE level at a time, so "Assets/A/B/C" has to be walked.
